content:
Sasha: Heads-up — int4 bring-up for aurora-lite-q5 is showing a locale-sensitive regression: JA/KO translation BLEU drop + embedding sim shift on kana-heavy inputs. Repro + short logs below.

Sasha: Repro command: 
```bash
python eval.py --model aurora-lite-q5-int4 --dataset wmt-ja-en-kor --split test --samples 400
```

Sasha: Quick numbers vs fp16 baseline: 
BLEU en->ja: 29.4 -> 24.7 (-4.7)
BLEU en->ko: 30.8 -> 26.9 (-3.9)
Mean src->hyp embed cos: 0.87 -> 0.73
Median token count +1.6 (extra subtokens around kana)

Hiro: That's larger than our usual quant noise. Any pattern on failing samples?

Sasha: Concentrated on subtitle/ruby cases and long kana runs. Also samples with invisible separators (ZWJ, ZWSP) and fullwidth punctuation look worse. Dumped a token/detok diff for one example: 

Sasha: ```
SRC: "She whispered, \"また明日、あやちゃん。\""
FP16-detok: "彼女は囁いた。\"また明日、あやちゃん。\""
INT4-detok: "彼女は囁いた。\"また明日、あややちゃん。\""
# int4 output has inserted embedded \u0000 (or invisible) characters near small kana clusters
```

Marta: Interesting — tokenizer pre-merge outputs match between fp16/int4, so this points to generation post-processing (detok) diverging. Could kernel selection reorder change token emission boundaries?

Tian: I suspect either kernel ordering or kvcache precision rounding (fp32->fp16) causing slightly different logits -> different argmaxs near subtoken boundaries. I can run a two-axis bisect (kernel A/B x kvcache rounding on/off) on the dev pool.

Sasha: Kicked off bisect job run-2026-03-20-aurora-int4-bisect-01 (https://ci.redwood/run/aurora-int4-bisect-01). It will record detok diffs and per-step token traces.

eval-bot: Queued run-2026-03-20-aurora-int4-bisect-01. Will post summaries after each pass.

Hiro: While Tian runs bisect, please add a detok smoke assert to fail if control/invisible chars (ZWSP/ZWNJ/null) appear in outputs for JA/KO promptsets. Also promote a small 200-sample kana+ruby promptset to high-sensitivity alerts.

Marta: On it. I'll add the assert to Redwood Optimize's smoke and add the kana promptset.

Sasha: Owner list: Tian - run bisect and post diffs; Marta - add detok asserts + promptset; Hiro - audit generation post-processing; Sasha - collect failing examples into a shared gist.

Tian: First bisect pass done: kernel ordering variant B reproduces the stray-invisible insertion, variant A matches fp16 detok. Posting diff snippet shortly.

Hiro: If kernel ordering B is the culprit, we should hold that ordering on production subtitle-heavy routes until we root cause.

Sasha: Agreed. Pausing aurora-lite int4 canary for subtitle routes. Will update once bisect finalizes. :thumbsup:
